sun.upright:
Nobody likes being told they got it wrong, and an Aries Sun likes it least of all. You want to be first, the one who moved while everyone else was still talking, and you want to be seen as someone who doesn't get knocked down. This is a Saturn card, and Saturn is in fall in Aries. The planet of limits and consequences gets less of a hearing in your sign than almost anywhere, so its lessons tend to reach you late and sideways, usually through somebody else. The card also comes from Libra, the sign directly opposite yours, the far end of your own axis, where partners and rivals live.

So whatever's hurting probably came from another person. Something was said, or a decision was made about you, and it cut into the thing you were proudest of. What you feel first is heat. You want to answer, win it back, prove them wrong by Friday. The sadness turns up later, in the car or at two in the morning, and it embarrasses you because it doesn't feel like strength. Air feeds fire, so every time you replay what they said, it burns a bit hotter.

At work it could be the pitch that got knocked back, or the job that went to someone you rate below yourself. With someone you love, it's the one line from the last argument you can't shake, because some of it was true. Write down the part that was fair. Keep the page, and don't answer anyone until you've read it back twice.
sun.reversed:
An Aries Sun with the Three the wrong way up tends to skip the hurt and head straight for the next thing. The disappointment becomes a plan, a new goal, a fight with somebody who had nothing to do with it. Saturn in fall already struggles to get a word in with Mars running the house, and reversed it hardly bothers trying. So the lesson goes unlearned and the same sort of blow keeps landing, dressed a little differently each time.

You'll see it in your working life as the fresh project started a week after the old one collapsed, with nothing learned carried over. In love it's a new person, quickly, or the old one blamed for everything. Your body keeps count even when you don't, usually as restless sleep and a short fuse with whoever's closest. Give yourself one quiet evening with no plan in it, and let whatever comes up come up.

moon.upright:
Anger is the feeling an Aries Moon can find fastest, and sadness is the one it trusts least. Drawn for your tides, this card says sadness is the one that's up. Something has hurt, in the soft place you don't show people. Saturn is in fall in Aries, which in plain terms means the slow, heavy side of feeling has no comfortable seat in your chart, so grief tends to come out of you as irritation, because that's the door that opens easiest.

It's confusing when it happens. You snap at someone over the washing up and realise halfway through the sentence that you're close to tears, and that makes you angrier. Libra sits opposite Aries, so this card comes from the relationship side of your wheel, and the hurt probably involves being let down by someone you'd let in. You need to act on a feeling before you feel safe with it. There's nothing to act on here, and that's the hard part. Air and fire get on, so the hurt catches quickly when it's talked about and flares, then burns down fast if you let it.

In a partnership it looks like the fight that isn't really about the dishes. In the body it's tight shoulders, a clenched jaw, a need to go for a hard run. With a friend it can be the message you're itching to send. Go for the run, by all means. When you get back, say the plain word for the feeling to someone you trust, even if the word is only 'hurt'.
moon.reversed:
A quarrel that keeps getting reopened is the usual shape of this card reversed on an Aries Moon. The hurt was real, and feeling that's ruled by Mars likes a target, so the wound gets picked at, brought up again, used as ammunition next time. Sometimes it goes the other way and the whole thing is stamped flat. You're fine, you've moved on, and you'll hear no more about it, thanks.

At home it surfaces as the old grievance that comes out whenever you're tired. With friends it might be a falling-out you tell as a funny story with an edge on it. Sleep gets broken by arguments you replay and win. When you feel yourself reaching for the old wound mid-row, stop and ask whether that's actually what you're upset about. Usually it isn't, and the real thing is smaller and easier to say.

rising.upright:
Picture Aries rising walking into a room with its chin up and a heart with three swords through it. That's roughly what this draw looks like from the outside. Your Ascendant meets the world head on, quick and direct, and people take you for someone who bounces back. With Aries rising, Libra is the sign on your seventh house, the house of other people, and this is a Libra card. So whatever cut you probably came through a partner, a rival, or someone you signed up to work with. Saturn's fall in Aries adds to it, since the sober part of the card has trouble getting past your front door.

There's a gap between how you come across and how you are. You still arrive first, still make the call, still get on with it, and a few people who know you well can see it's costing you. Strangers mostly can't. The instinct is to lead with toughness and get the first word in, so nobody else gets to say the hard thing. Air fans fire, and brisk can tip into sharp without you meaning it.

In a new job it might be the colleague who asks an innocent question and gets a clipped answer. Meeting someone new romantically, it's the joke about your ex that comes out too fast. With an old friend at the pub, it's being unusually quiet. Who would you let see that you're sore? Pick one of them and let them.
rising.reversed:
Armour is the first thing people meet when this card turns over on an Aries Ascendant. You don't want anyone asking, so you move fast and talk over the quiet moments, and the speed reads as bluntness. Saturn in fall gives the part of you that would pause and weigh things very little say. Or the hurt breaks through at the worst time, a flash of temper at a stranger over nothing much, a parking space or a queue.

New colleagues may decide you're hard work before they've seen the rest of you. A date may find you good company and oddly shut, and not know why. Even the barista gets a shorter answer than they deserve. Slow the first minute of any meeting right down. Say hello properly, ask one question, and let the other person finish their answer before you move on to business.

sun.upright:
Something you put years into hasn't held, or won't hold in the shape you wanted. Taurus Suns build slowly and expect what they build to still be standing in a decade, so this lands hard. The card is air and your Sun is earth, and those two elements are opposed, talk against proof. You trust what you can touch, the house, the account, the relationship you've kept going for years. Words and truths feel flimsy to you right up until one of them lands.

Saturn has no dignity in Taurus. It's Venus's guest there, and it arrives in your chart looking for what's worth keeping. It does have a foothold in your sign, though, because it rules the last ten degrees of Taurus, the decan of the Seven of Pentacles, the gardener leaning on a hoe and looking at a crop that's taken ages. That's the feeling here. You've waited and tended, and you're having to look honestly at what came up. You don't cry easily. Likelier you'll feel tired and flat for weeks and not connect it to anything.

With money it might be an investment, a business or a savings plan that didn't pay back what went in. In love it could be a long relationship where you finally admit one of you stopped trying some time ago. In a job it's the one you stayed in for security. Make a proper list of what's still yours, all of it, people included, and put it on the fridge.
sun.reversed:
A Taurus Sun with the card reversed tends to sit on the hurt. Fixed earth is very good at not moving, and that includes not moving through a loss. You keep the arrangement going because stopping would mean admitting it's over, so it carries on in name while everyone involved knows it isn't working. Sometimes comfort takes the place of grief. The good bottle opened a bit too often, the takeaway, a sofa you don't get off.

In a job it shows as loyalty to a boss who stopped being loyal back some time ago. In a relationship it's staying put, polite and settled and unhappy. With money it's hanging onto something that's losing value because selling feels like failing. Name one thing you're keeping mainly out of habit, and set a date to decide about it.

moon.upright:
Comfort for a Taurus Moon is food, warmth, a familiar bed and the same few people. So when this card falls on your Moon it tends to land in the body first. Something hurt, and you can feel it as a weight in your chest or a loss of appetite well before you've found words for it. The card is air, your Moon is earth, and those elements don't much like each other. Feeling for you is physical and slow, and this card arrives with a sharp, spoken kind of pain, a sentence someone said, a message on a screen.

Libra and Taurus are quincunx as well, the awkward angle, two signs with nothing in common that keep having to adjust. You might not be able to talk about the hurt at all, and people who try to help by talking about it may make it worse. There's one kindness in the chart for you. Venus rules Taurus, and Saturn is her guest here, so the card is gentler with you than it looks. It wants the grief looked after the way you'd look after anything precious, slowly, with good things around it.

In the kitchen it might be cooking big meals and eating none of them, or all of them. With someone you love it's wanting to be held and not asked anything. Sleep tends to go long and heavy. Let yourself have the comfort, and pair it with one short sentence to one person about what's actually wrong. That's enough talking for a while.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, the card on a Taurus Moon usually means a hurt that's settled into the body and stayed. Fixed earth can hold a feeling for a very long time without letting on, and the grief goes somewhere quieter. A heaviness that won't lift, habits that got bigger, a stubborn cheerfulness nobody is allowed to question.

It shows in the pantry and the shopping, in evenings that all look the same, and in the way every conversation gets steered away from the one subject. A partner may feel they're living beside a closed door. Try moving the grief physically. A long, slow walk somewhere you went with the person or the thing you lost, with nothing to get back for, will often shift more than any conversation.

rising.upright:
Nobody meeting you would guess anything was wrong, and that's worth noticing. Taurus rising looks unshakeable. People see steadiness, good manners, someone who won't be rushed, and they assume you're fine. Saturn's only standing in your sign is its decan at the far end of Taurus, the Seven of Pentacles, and otherwise it's a visitor taking its manners from Venus, so it keeps its sadness polite. The card's air against your earth means the painful thing probably arrived as words, and your calm face is how you answer words, with something solid.

You'll know the moment. Someone asks how you are and you say 'good, thanks' with complete conviction and a slight lump in your throat. Libra and Taurus sit at a quincunx, so there's a constant small adjustment going on between what you feel and what you're willing to show, and it's tiring in a way nobody else sees. Because you look calm, people also bring you their bad news, and you end up being the steady one for others while carrying something yourself.

At work you might be the one asked to break difficult news to the team because you seem unflappable. Starting something new, a class or a club, you'll be pleasant and a bit closed. Dating, you'll come across as easy company and hard to know. Once, soon, when someone asks how you are, give them the true answer in one sentence.
rising.reversed:
The calm can set hard on a Taurus Ascendant when this card is reversed. You look perfectly fine and entirely out of reach, and people give up asking. Or something small cracks it in public, a kind word from a stranger, a song playing in a shop, and the grief comes out somewhere you'd never have chosen.

A colleague may assume you don't care because you never react. New people like you and stay at a distance, because you haven't offered anything to get hold of. At a family gathering it's the stiff politeness while the hurt sits at the table with you. Choose somewhere private and safe to let the face drop for an hour, alone or with one person, so it doesn't have to drop in the supermarket.

sun.upright:
Both of these are air signs, Libra and Gemini, four signs apart in a trine, so this card speaks your language almost too well. Gemini Suns are here to find things out and pass them on. You like being quick and in the know, the one who understood first. Same element means it all gets louder, and the pain in this card is a thinking kind of pain. Something you learned, a sentence you read, a truth that clicked into place and now can't be unclicked.

Saturn has no rank in Gemini. It takes its colour from Mercury, which makes it talkative and curious, restless even when it's sad. So you'll probably understand the hurt very well. You can tell the whole story with the timeline and the reasons, and you may have told it several times already. What the card wants is harder for a Gemini. It wants you to let the fact be true without doing anything clever with it. Your sign's own card is The Lovers, which is about a choice, and there's often a choice folded into this hurt, something you have to stop keeping your options open about.

At work it could be finding out about a decision everyone else knew before you. With a sibling or an old friend, it might be the conversation that showed they see you differently from how you'd thought. With a partner it's reading something you weren't meant to read. Choose what you're going to do about it, one thing, and tell only the person it affects.
sun.reversed:
A Gemini Sun with this card reversed turns the hurt into material. It becomes a funny story, a clever take, a long thread of messages, and every retelling moves it further from what actually happened to you. Mercury's quickness gets used to stay one step ahead of the feeling. You're busy, you're sociable, and you're never quite alone with it.

Friends find you great company and have no idea how you really are. Work gets three new projects the week after a disappointment, so there's no gap. In a relationship the subject changes every time it comes close. Try telling the story once without a single joke in it. Say it slowly, to someone who won't laugh, and notice where your voice goes.

moon.upright:
What settles a Gemini Moon is talking. A friend on the phone, a long voice note, working it out loud until the feeling makes sense. With this card drawn for your tides, something has hurt, and it's probably come in through words. A message, a comment, something overheard. Libra and Gemini share an element and sit in an easy trine, so the card goes straight into your emotional wiring, and it can bring clarity or a loop that won't stop.

The trouble with air meeting air is that everything echoes. You reread the message. You rewrite what you should have said. You explain the whole thing to three friends and ask each of them what they think it meant, and by evening it's bigger than it was. Saturn is only a visitor in Gemini, borrowing Mercury's manner, so the heaviness in this card comes out in your head as restlessness and busy thinking, and much less as tears. You need company for your thoughts, and a few of these thoughts are better left alone for a day or two.

Sleep shows it first, often as a late night on the phone. With a sibling or close friend, it's the one person whose view you trust and the pull to keep asking them. With a partner it could be a sentence of theirs you keep turning over. Put the phone in another room for one evening. Write down what hurt, in full, on paper, and show it to nobody.
moon.reversed:
Busy is how a Gemini Moon goes numb, and with the Three reversed that's usually what's happening. The feeling is there, but it never gets a quiet minute to land, because there's always another tab, another podcast, another plan for Saturday. Saturn in Mercury's sign gets scattered, and the grief breaks into little pieces that are easier to ignore one at a time.

You'll see it in how much you're on the phone, especially late. With friends there's a lot of chat and very little said. On family calls you're relentlessly cheerful. Sometimes it flips and you're stuck on one line someone said months ago, replaying it word for word. Give it a set time either way. Ten minutes, a timer, a chair, and you let yourself feel whatever's there until it goes off, and then you get up.

rising.upright:
Words are doing the damage in this draw, one way or another. Gemini rising opens with talk, light and quick and curious, the person who asks where you got your jacket and what you do and whether you've read that thing. With this card at your door, you might be the one who's said something sharp and true to someone who wasn't ready. Or a stranger's remark has gone straight in. Air and air in a trine means nothing slows it down, and things said at the door get through fast.

Saturn is a visitor in Gemini, taking on Mercury's tone, and it gives your usual lightness a heavier edge. People might notice you're a touch more serious, a little slower with the joke. It can feel like you've lost your knack for small talk, as if the patter's gone flat. That's worth listening to. There may be one honest thing you want to say at the start of conversations, and the chatter is getting in its way.

In a job interview it could be the moment you tell the truth about why you left the last place. With a new friend it's the day you say something real and they either lean in or don't. Online it's worth checking whether the witty line is kinder in your head than on the screen. Before you post or send anything clever, read it back once as if you were the person it's about.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, the card can make a Gemini Ascendant sharper than you mean to be. The quick remark comes out with an edge, the joke lands on someone's sore spot, and because you're already onto the next thing you don't see it land. Or the hurt makes you flippant, and you make light of everything so nobody can tell that something wasn't light at all.

In a meeting it's the comment that gets repeated back to you later, less funny out of context. With someone new it's banter that keeps them at arm's length. Online it's the reply fired off too fast. Slow your first sentences down with new people for a while. If something you're about to say is funny mostly because it stings, keep it for your own notes.

sun.upright:
The hurt in this card has landed close to home, which for a Cancer Sun is the worst place it could land. You're building a place where people are safe, and you want to be known as the one who made it. Saturn is in detriment in your sign. It sits opposite Capricorn, its home, so the planet of hard edges has to work in the softest sign there is, and the effort shows. That gives the Three of Swords extra weight for you. A hurt in the family, a home that didn't stay the way you hoped, someone you protected who didn't protect you back.

Libra squares Cancer. Both are cardinal signs that like to start things, and the friction between them forces action, so this isn't one you can wait out. It's a strange mix. Part of you wants to pull everyone close and fix it, and part of you wants to go to your room and not come out. Your sign's card is The Chariot, the figure in armour driving forward, and that's often what a Cancer Sun does in a crisis. You organise, drive, hold it together for everyone, and find your own hurt waiting at the end of the week, untouched.

With a parent it might be a conversation that finally said something true about your childhood. With your own children, or anyone you mind like a child, it's seeing them hurt and not being able to stop it. At home it could be a move, or a change in who lives there. Let one person look after you for a change. Tell them exactly what would help.
sun.reversed:
When the card reverses for a Cancer Sun, the hurt goes into the shell. You carry on caring for everyone, making the dinners, remembering the birthdays, and privately you're keeping count of how little comes back. Saturn in detriment turned inwards can make grief quietly bitter. It isn't loud. It comes out as sighs, and as 'it's fine' said a lot.

In the family it's being the one who holds everything together and resenting it a bit more each month. With a partner it's the hurt they don't know about because you've never actually said it. At work it can be looking after a team better than you look after yourself. Say one of the hurts out loud to the person it's about. Keep it short, and don't apologise for raising it.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon feels things at full strength with memory attached. Here a present hurt is pulling older ones up behind it. You might notice that something small, a missed phone call or an offhand remark, has set off a sadness far too big for it. That's Saturn's doing. It's in detriment in Cancer, heavy-footed and out of place, and it has a way of bringing up what's been stored.

Air and water have no natural bond, so the facts of what happened can be perfectly clear while your feelings about them won't line up. You know it was fair. You know nobody meant harm. You're still in tears at the kitchen bench. The square between Libra and Cancer makes it a pressure you can't sleep off, and in the end it asks you to do something with the feeling, however small.

With your mother, or whoever mothered you, it could be an old wound opening again, and that needn't mean the relationship is worse. Around the house it might be clearing out a room or a box of things. Your stomach and your sleep will probably tell you before your head does. Write to the person you've been missing, even if you don't send it, and keep the letter.
moon.reversed:
A Cancer Moon with this card reversed tends to hold on. The old texts are still on the phone, the jumper's still in the drawer, and you know the dates by heart. There's tenderness in that, and there's also a way of keeping the wound open because closing it would feel like forgetting. Saturn in detriment can make grief feel like loyalty.

It shows at home in rooms left as they were and plans put off. In friendships it might be bringing the conversation back to the loss when others have moved on, and feeling hurt again when they don't follow. Choose one object connected to the hurt and decide what to do with it. Keep it somewhere special, give it away, or put it out of sight. Any of those is fine, as long as you choose.

rising.upright:
You're the one who offers the tea, notices who's uncomfortable and reads a room before stepping into it. That's Cancer rising, and with this card drawn for your mask, you're meeting the world with something sore that careful people will see. Cancer's ruler is the Moon, and a Cancer Ascendant's feelings show on the face more than you'd like. Saturn's in detriment on your Ascendant, awkward and heavy at the front of the chart, so the hurt is hard to hide behind good manners.

Libra and Cancer square each other, two cardinal signs that both want to start things and want to start them differently. So there's a push and pull in how you greet people. Part of you wants to open up to the first kind face, and part of you wants to scuttle back into the shell. With Cancer rising, Libra is also your fourth-house sign, which puts this card at the roots of your chart. Whatever's hurting is likely to be tied to home, family, or where you live.

At work you may be more easily wounded by a brisk email. At a party you might go quiet and leave early. With new people it's worth noticing who you trust and why. If one person has shown they can hold something gently, let them see a bit of what's going on. Everyone else can have the tea.
rising.reversed:
Invitations get declined when Cancer rising has this card reversed. You meet new people with a polite, closed face and go sideways round any question that gets near the sore spot. Saturn in detriment on your Ascendant makes the armour heavier than it needs to be. Or the hurt leaks out defensively, a snap at someone who meant well, followed by a long apology in your head.

At work this can look like distance from a team you usually mother. Among friends it's the muted group chat and the catch-up you keep moving. With family it might be staying away from gatherings where you'd have to answer questions. Pick the one person who'd understand without needing the whole story. Meet them somewhere easy, their kitchen or a walk, and let them ask one question.

sun.upright:
Pride is where this one lands first. Leo Suns want to make something that's theirs and be loved for it, and the Three of Swords comes straight at that. Leo is the sign opposite Aquarius, one of Saturn's two homes, which puts Saturn in its detriment here. In the Sun's own sign it feels like a cold draught in a warm room. It asks whether the thing you're proud of is as strong as you thought, and it picks a bad moment to ask. The card's air fans your fire, so the hurt is quick and bright and very hard to ignore.

Saturn does have a foothold in your sign. It rules the first ten degrees of Leo, the decan of the Five of Wands, five lads swinging staves in a scrap nobody seems to be winning. So the hurt may have come out of competition, or a squabble where your pride took a knock. A Leo Sun feels this as wounded dignity. You were generous, you put your heart into it, and it wasn't enough, or somebody else got the credit, or the applause didn't come. There's a real sorrow under that, and pride tends to cover it with something grand.

Creatively it might be a piece of work that was turned down or ignored. In romance it's being loved less than you love, which is close to the worst hurt a Leo knows. With children, your own or ones you care about, it's the day they pulled away a little. Let someone see you disappointed without dressing it up. One friend, one honest conversation, no performance.
sun.reversed:
A Leo Sun with the card upside down either makes the hurt into a show or refuses to show it at all. Both are pride. There's a big scene and everyone knows you've been wronged, or you're glowing and generous in public while the wound sits untended at home. Saturn is uncomfortable in your sign at the best of times, and reversed it gets pushed right out of view.

In your work it can look like going cold on a project the moment it stopped being praised. With a partner it's a hurt turned into a test, waiting to see whether they notice. With friends it's the breakup told as a triumph. Tell one person the unflattering version, the one where you were sad and a bit foolish and wanted to be chosen. It usually comes as a relief to say it.

moon.upright:
Somebody's warmth has gone cool, or you've found out it wasn't quite what you believed. For a Leo Moon that's about as bad as news gets, because warmth aimed at you is what you run on. Being noticed, being chosen, having someone's face light up when you walk in. Saturn is out of its element in Leo, in its detriment, and emotionally that feels like the heating's been switched off. The planet of distance and limits is sitting in the one sign the Sun runs, so the hurt has a chill in it.

The card is air and your Moon is fire, and air feeds fire, so the feeling is big. You won't do this quietly, and there's no reason you should. The harder part is that fixed fire holds on. A Leo Moon can stay loyal to a person or a hope long after it's stopped giving anything back. That loyalty feels like love, and some of it is. Some of it is pride that doesn't want to admit being left out in the cold.

With a partner it could be the evening you realised they'd stopped looking at you the way they used to. With friends it's not being invited, and minding more than you'd say. The body carries it as restlessness at night and a heaviness in the chest. Libra is sextile Leo, an easy opening that still needs using, and here it means friends are closer to hand than you think. Ring the warmest person you know and tell them you're low.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on a Leo Moon, the hurt can turn into sulking on a grand scale. You withdraw the warmth to show them what it's like, and you wait to be coaxed back. Or you throw yourself into being the life of every party so nobody guesses, which works for a night and leaves you flat for three. Saturn out of place in Leo, and reversed as well, makes it very hard to ask for anything directly.

At home it's the silent treatment, dignified and total. With friends it's generosity with an edge, gifts and invitations that are partly a test. Sleep may go late and restless. The hurt usually softens faster once you name what you wanted, which is often just to be picked first. Say that to the person, plainly. Most people find it easier to answer than a mood.

rising.upright:
Leo rising arrives warm and generous and slightly on show, and people expect sunshine from you. With this card on your Ascendant, there's a dimmer light behind the usual brightness, and some people will notice. Saturn's detriment in Leo puts the planet of restraint uncomfortably in charge of how you come across. You might find you can't quite summon the usual shine, which is a strange experience for a Leo Ascendant.

The sextile between Libra and Leo helps a little. It's an easy link, and with Leo rising, Libra falls in your third house, the house of everyday talk, so conversations with people close by are where this card is doing its work. Something may have been said to you in passing that cut. Or you're the one who needs to say something honest, in a casual setting, and the words won't fit your usual cheerful manner. Saturn's decan in your sign, the Five of Wands, adds some friction to first meetings, the sense of being sized up.

At work the brave face is taking a lot of energy to keep up. In a new relationship you might be hiding a recent hurt behind charm. With neighbours or siblings, a short chat in the hallway can land heavily. Turn down one thing that needs you to perform, and spend that evening with someone who doesn't need the show.
rising.reversed:
The performance goes up a notch when a Leo Ascendant gets this card reversed. You're brighter, louder and funnier than you feel, and it's a lot of work to keep that up in every room. People mostly buy it. The ones who know you notice the smile hasn't reached your eyes.

At work it might be over-volunteering, being seen to cope magnificently. Socially it's arriving big and leaving early, exhausted. In a new romance it's hiding a recent hurt behind so much charm that the whole thing feels slightly unreal to the other person. Saturn reversed in Leo tends to make you proud of not needing anything. Try needing something small and asking for it, a lift, an hour, a phone call, and see who turns up.

sun.upright:
A mistake that mattered, criticism that was fair, a job done properly that nobody valued. The Three of Swords usually finds a Virgo Sun through the work, or through the part of you that measures yourself by it. You want to be useful and to get things right. Libra and Virgo sit side by side, neighbours with little in common. Libra has the grace and the sense of what's fair to others, and Virgo has the craft and the standards. This card asks you to borrow some of Libra's fairness and point it at yourself.

The card is air and your Sun is earth, idea against matter. Saturn has no dignity in Virgo and picks up the colouring of your ruler, Mercury, so this becomes a very thinking kind of hurt. You'll go over it and over it. What should you have done, where did it start going wrong, who knew before you did. It feels like responsibility. A lot of the time it's a way of having the hurt without being sad, because sad isn't useful and analysis is. I've seen plenty of Virgos turn grief into a to-do list.

In a job it might be a review or a piece of feedback that stung. In the body it's often the gut, and sleep that breaks at four. In a relationship it could be hearing that your care felt like criticism to someone. Pick the one thing you'd genuinely do differently. Write that down, and let the rest of the list go.
sun.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Virgo Sun can get stuck in the audit. You keep going over what went wrong, and the grief turns into a long private case against yourself. Or it turns outwards and you start correcting everyone else's small mistakes because you can't touch the big one. Saturn shaped by Mercury, with nowhere useful to go, gets fussy and sharp.

In the office that looks like perfectionism that slows everything down and helps nobody. At home it might be cleaning the oven at eleven at night. With a partner it's criticism coming out when what you mean is that you're hurt. Give yourself one day of doing things at eighty per cent. Leave something imperfect on purpose, and let yourself be sad about the real thing instead.

moon.upright:
The bench is wiped, the week's planned, and it hasn't helped. A Virgo Moon feels safe when life is in order, and when this card falls here, something has come in that won't be put in order. A loss, a painful truth, a thing somebody said. Your first instinct will be to organise around it, and that's fine. It's how this Moon copes, and it does help. It just doesn't reach all the way down.

Libra and Virgo are neighbours, a semi-sextile, and neighbouring signs rarely understand each other. The card's Saturn has no dignity in Virgo. It's shaped by Mercury, your Moon's ruler, so the hurt shows up as thoughts, lists and worries, a quiet commentary on what you should have noticed. Air against earth is felt as a gap between knowing and feeling. You know exactly what happened. Your body is still catching up, and it'll let you know with a tight stomach, a stiff neck, an urge to scrub something.

The house might be spotless while your appetite has gone. With a partner it's being extremely helpful and very hard to comfort. With a friend who's also hurting, you might look after them so you don't have to look at your own. Make one space in the day where nothing gets fixed. Sit with a cup of tea and do nothing useful for twenty minutes.
moon.reversed:
Worry takes over for a Virgo Moon when this card is reversed. The hurt gets broken into so many small problems that you never feel the whole of it. Your health, the money, whether that email sounded rude, and underneath all of it a sadness that hasn't been given any time at all.

It usually shows in the body first, tension, restless sleep, that tired and wired feeling. In a relationship it might be picking at your partner over small things. At work it's staying late to fix what didn't need fixing. Try naming the sadness in plain words, once. 'I'm sad about' and then the actual thing. Say it out loud to someone, or to the empty kitchen if nobody's around.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising comes across as capable and a bit reserved. People trust you with the details and assume you've got things handled. With this card drawn for your mask, what they're actually meeting is someone quietly sore, holding it together with good manners and a well-kept diary. Saturn is only a visitor in Virgo, coloured by Mercury, so the hurt shows in how you talk more than in your face. You're a touch more precise, more careful with your words, a little stiff.

The Libra card and your Virgo Ascendant are neighbours, and with Virgo rising, Libra is the sign on your second house, the house of money and what you value. So there may be a practical side to this hurt, something about money or worth or what you're prepared to put up with. The card is air against your earth, which suggests the thing that hurt was an idea or a sentence, and you're answering it with competence. The Hermit is Virgo's card, the old man alone with his lamp, and you'll want time on your own to sort it out.

In a job interview you'll probably be very good and a bit guarded. In a new friendship you might seem kind and slightly unreachable. With money, after being let down, you're likely to be extra careful. Ask yourself who you've been most polite with lately, and whether that politeness is covering a hurt they'd want to know about.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, the card can make a Virgo Ascendant brittle. The polite, capable front gets stiffer, and small things set you off, a typo, a late reply, someone asking the obvious. People may read you as critical or cold when you're really hurting and trying to keep everything exactly in place so nothing else goes wrong.

With a colleague it's a curt reply that surprises you both. On a first date it's coming across as fussy because your attention went to the menu. With family it's one small correction too many. When you notice yourself tightening up in company, drop your jaw and your shoulders on purpose, and say something warm before you say anything useful.

sun.upright:
This card belongs to your sign. The Three of Swords is the second decan of Libra, the ten degrees in the middle, and it's ruled by Saturn, which is exalted in Libra, at its most idealised, the planet of commitment wanting things to be truly fair. So for a Libra Sun this is heartbreak in your own language. A relationship, a partnership, a question of who owes what to whom. Libra's Major is Justice, a figure with a sword and scales, and that sword isn't far from these three.

Libra Suns are here to make things balanced and lovely and to be seen as fair. The painful part is that this card asks for a judgement, and judgements aren't always kind. Same sign, same element, and that turns everything up, for better and for too much. You'll probably see every side of what happened, theirs included, and still feel cut. That's allowed. Understanding why someone hurt you doesn't stop it hurting. What it feels like is a kind of tired clarity, the moment you stop arguing with the truth.

In a relationship this might mean admitting something isn't working, or hearing the other person admit it. In business it's a partnership where the terms were never really equal. With friends it's the one who has always taken a little more than they gave. Say out loud, to whoever needs to hear it, what would make this fair. Stick to that and leave out the apology.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun with this card reversed usually keeps the peace at its own expense. You can see the truth plainly and still won't say it, because saying it would upset someone, and you'd sooner be unhappy and liked. Saturn is strong in your sign, and reversed that strength turns into endurance. The relationship carries on, the arrangement holds, and the unfairness runs for another year.

In a partnership it's the talk you keep saving for the right moment. At work it's covering for a colleague who doesn't pull their weight. With friends it's the group you stay in because leaving would cause a fuss. Write down what you'd say if you weren't worried about the reaction. Read it the next morning and decide whether any of it needs saying out loud.

moon.upright:
Harmony is what a Libra Moon needs to feel safe. People getting along, a home that looks nice, no raised voices. With this card on your Moon the peace has been broken, and probably in a close bond. The card is one of Libra's own, the middle ten degrees, and Saturn, which rules it, is exalted in your sign. Emotionally that means the hurt has a certain justice to it. Something true has come out, and part of you knows it had to.

You'll think about it a lot, and a Libra Moon thinks about feelings through other people. What they said, what they meant, whether they're alright. That's your gift and also the snag. You can spend so long understanding the other side that your own hurt never gets a turn. It feels like being fair, and some of it is avoidance. You'd prefer to be the reasonable one, because the sad one is less pleasant to be around, and pleasantness matters to you. I see this a lot with Libra Moons.

In a partnership it could be the quiet after an honest conversation. With friends it might be discovering someone has been talking about you. Sleep may be light, and you'll want the room just so before you can drop off. For one day, stop being fair about it. Be on your own side completely, say so to one person, and see how that feels.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Libra Moon tends to smooth things over too fast. The hurt gets tidied away before it's been felt, the apology accepted before it's been made, and the dinner party goes ahead. Saturn exalted in your sign wants honesty, and turned inwards it becomes a very polite resentment with nowhere to go.

In a relationship you'll see it as agreeing to everything and quietly withdrawing. With friends it's being lovely to someone who hurt you and feeling worse after every visit. The body keeps it in tight shoulders. Pick the relationship where you've smoothed the most, and let one small true thing come out a bit rough. Say it at a calm moment, in plain words, and let the silence after it sit there.

rising.upright:
Libra rising has a gracious way with strangers. You put people at ease, you find the nice thing to say, and first meetings usually go well. This card on your Ascendant is standing in its own doorway, since it's one of Libra's three decans and Saturn is exalted there. So a deeply Libran kind of hurt is showing in how you meet people, a bond that broke or a fairness that failed, and your charm is working harder than usual to carry it.

Libra is cardinal, a starting sign, and Libra rising starts things through other people. Meeting someone, agreeing something, joining up. When a partnership has just hurt you, that way in feels risky. You might be a little more careful with new people, slower to trust someone who's lovely straight away. Your sense of what's fair is sharp, and with air doubled up, so is your sensitivity to anything that isn't. You'll clock the slight in a stranger's tone within seconds.

In a new job it could show as being more reserved in team settings, watching who's reliable. Dating after a breakup, it's the first coffee where you're charming and completely guarded. With neighbours and acquaintances, small talk feels like hard work. It's fine to be less agreeable for a while. Notice who stays warm when you're not doing all the work, and spend more time with them.
rising.reversed:
Reversed on a Libra Ascendant, the card can make the charm go mechanical. You smile, say the right things, agree with everyone, and none of it touches what's actually going on. People like you and feel they haven't met you. Or the hurt makes you unusually blunt, and a Libra rising who's suddenly sharp shocks people in a way other signs wouldn't.

At work it's being the peacemaker for everyone else while quietly fuming. In a new relationship it's being so accommodating that the other person has no idea what you want. At social things it's the fixed smile that leaves your face aching on the drive home. Let one first meeting go a bit awkwardly on purpose. Disagree with something small and see what happens.

sun.upright:
Something's been found out. Maybe you found it, maybe it found you, and either way it's cut deep. Scorpio Suns want the truth, all of it, and they want to be known as the one who can't be fooled. Saturn has no dignity in Scorpio. It's a guest there and takes its colouring from Mars, or from Pluto if you use the modern ruler, which makes this card sharper and more personal for you. It feels like a wound with a name on it.

Libra and Scorpio are neighbours, a semi-sextile, and they have very different ideas about relationships. Libra wants things fair and balanced. Scorpio wants them all or nothing. The hurt often comes out of that gap, a partner who was being reasonable while you were being loyal. A Scorpio Sun experiences this as betrayal whether or not it strictly was one. There might be a cold, clear anger, and a pull to close off completely, and underneath both a grief you don't let anyone near.

In a relationship it could be learning something about a partner or friend that changes the picture. With shared money it might be discovering the arrangement wasn't what you'd been told. At work it's losing an ally. Scorpio's card is Death, which is about endings that make room. Ask yourself honestly whether this is something to repair or something to end, and give it a week before you act on the answer.
sun.reversed:
When the card turns over for a Scorpio Sun, the hurt tends to go underground and stay there. You don't forgive, you don't forget, and you don't talk about it either. Saturn coloured by Mars can hold a grudge with great patience. It can look like strength. Often it's a wound that's never been let out into the air, and this is an air card.

In a workplace it might be a cold war with a former ally that everyone can feel. In love it's testing a new partner for the betrayal the last one committed. In the family it's the name nobody mentions. Ask whether holding on is protecting you or keeping you tied to the person who hurt you. If it's the second, find a way to say your piece, in person or on paper, and then stop carrying it.

moon.upright:
The Three of Swords on a Scorpio Moon goes deep and stays private. You feel everything at full strength and choose very carefully who gets to see it. What you need is loyalty and honesty, and this card usually means one of those has been broken, or a truth has come out that's rearranged how safe you feel with someone. Scorpio is fixed water, ruled by Mars and in modern astrology by Pluto, and neither of those is a light touch.

Air and water are neutral to each other, so the card's clear, spoken truth and your deep, wordless feeling don't automatically fit. You might know exactly what happened and still find the feeling has a life of its own, surfacing at night, in dreams, in a sudden wave in the shower. Saturn, a visitor in Scorpio, gives it weight and staying power. This won't be done by the weekend. It can feel like your body is guarding something, as if one wrong move could set it off.

In intimacy it may be hard to be touched or close for a while, and that's worth saying gently to a partner. With shared money, or trust around it, there could be a rethink. In the family an old loyalty or secret may be shifting. Choose one person you trust completely and tell them the whole thing, the petty bits and the frightening bits too. Everyone else can stay on a need-to-know basis.
moon.reversed:
Brooding is the usual form this takes on a Scorpio Moon with the card reversed. You go over the hurt again and again, sometimes checking the other person's socials, sometimes rehearsing what you'd say. The wound stays open because you keep pressing on it to make sure it's still there. Or the whole thing is sealed behind a very calm face and nobody, you included, is allowed to look.

At home it's a heavy silence everyone feels and nobody names. In love it's jealousy that's hard to reason with. Sleep breaks up, with vivid dreams. Give the brooding a physical outlet. Swim, walk, lift something heavy, anything that tires the body enough for the mind to rest. And block the account you keep checking, at least for a month.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising already comes across as intense. People feel you watching and sense there's more going on than you're saying, and they're usually right. This time what's behind the stare is a hurt, and people may pick up on it quicker than usual. With Scorpio rising, Libra is the sign on your twelfth house, the hidden house, since the two signs sit side by side. That's where this card comes from for you. Whatever's hurting is probably something you don't talk about, and the card is bringing it up into how you meet the world.

Saturn has no special standing in Scorpio, and it takes its tone from Mars, your Ascendant's traditional ruler. So there's an edge to how you're coming across, more guarded, maybe a bit cutting in conversation. You might feel exposed, as if people can see through you, and that makes you want to shut down further. Air and water don't mix easily. The words for what's happened may not come, and that's alright.

At work people may give you a wide berth, and you might be glad of it. In new friendships you'll be slower to open up than usual. In dating it's hard to be light when something heavy is in the room. You don't owe anyone the whole story. Tell one person you already trust a small true part of it, and let that be enough.
rising.reversed:
When this card reverses on a Scorpio Ascendant, the guard goes all the way up. You meet everyone with a level look and give nothing away, and people find you hard to read. Some find you frightening. Saturn borrowing Mars's temper makes it very easy to strike first. Or there's a flash of sting, a remark that cuts too deep at a moment when nobody was expecting it.

On a team it's the colleague who's decided you're hostile and tells others so. In new relationships it's testing people so hard that they fail. With old friends it's missing the chance to be looked after. Let one person catch you on a soft day, without explaining or apologising. Let them make you a cup of tea, and drink it.

sun.upright:
A belief has taken a hit. A teacher, a cause, a plan for the future, a person you thought saw the world the way you do, and it's turned out otherwise. Sagittarius Suns are here to find meaning and chase it, preferably somewhere far away with good company. Saturn has no rank in Sagittarius. It's Jupiter's guest there, and Jupiter makes everything bigger, so a disappointment can feel as if it's taken your whole outlook down with it.

Libra and Sagittarius are sextile, a friendly link, air feeding fire, and it gives you a way through. You tend to recover by understanding, by finding a bigger picture where the hurt makes sense. Saturn also rules the last ten degrees of your sign, the Ten of Wands, someone bent double carrying a bundle of sticks into town. That's the other side of this. You may have been carrying more than your share of a belief or a project for a long time, and the heartbreak is partly exhaustion. Sadness can feel claustrophobic to a Sagittarius Sun. You want to get out, go somewhere, laugh about it, and some of that is healthy.

In study or travel it might be a course, a trip or a move that didn't work out. With a mentor or someone you looked up to, it's seeing their limits clearly. At work it's a mission statement you no longer believe. Pick one thing you're carrying out of duty to a belief you've outgrown, and put it down.
sun.reversed:
Silver linings come too quickly for a Sagittarius Sun with this card reversed. Everything happens for a reason, it was meant to be, onwards. Jupiter's optimism gets used to skip the sad part, and the lesson Saturn was bringing goes unread. Or the hurt turns into a crusade, and you become very outspoken about the thing that let you down, so everybody hears about it.

In your plans it's booking the big trip or starting the new course before the old disappointment has gone cold. With friends it's the funny version of events that hides the sore one. At work it can be loud criticism of an organisation you've already left in your heart. Before the next big change, give yourself one week in the ordinary life you've got, sad and bored and unremarkable, and see what comes up.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room to move and something to look forward to. When this card falls on your Moon, that sense of room has shrunk. A hope has been knocked back, or someone you trusted turned out to be smaller than you'd thought. Jupiter rules Sagittarius, and the card's Saturn is only a guest there, so the hurt takes on Jupiter's scale. It feels big and philosophical, as though it says something about how life works.

Air and fire are friendly elements that feed each other, and things move fast between them. You'll probably feel this strongly and briefly, a proper cry and then the urge to get out of the house. The trouble is that a Sagittarius Moon tends to leave before the feeling's finished. You go for the long drive, the weekend away, the fresh start, and the hurt comes along in the boot. Temperance is your sign's card, the angel pouring from one cup into another, and it points to a slower way, a little at a time.

With a partner it might look like needing space while they want to talk. With friends it's being the life of the evening and quiet on the drive home. Your body will want to move, and walking genuinely helps this Moon. Walk somewhere far, on your own, and let yourself be sad the whole way there and back. Make no plans on the walk.
moon.reversed:
When the card reverses on a Sagittarius Moon, restlessness often stands in for grief. You're booking things, changing things, suddenly desperate to be somewhere else, and none of it lifts the mood. Or the optimism tips into bluntness, and you say hurtful true things to the people around you because you're hurting and can't find anywhere else to put it.

At home it usually shows as not being there much. With a partner it's the hard truth delivered at the wrong moment. With friends it's a round of plans that leaves you worn out. Sit still for an evening. Tell someone the sad thing, then the part you're afraid it means about the future, and let them answer before you change the subject.

rising.upright:
You may be the one holding the sword this time. Sagittarius rising comes in friendly and a bit loud, ready with a joke and an opinion, and your honesty is part of the charm. There's a chance it's recently landed harder than you meant. Or the world's been blunt back, and a stranger's frank remark has knocked your good cheer sideways. Libra and Sagittarius are sextile, an easy link, and with Sagittarius rising Libra falls on your eleventh house, the house of friends and groups. So what hurts may have happened in a circle, a group of mates, a club, a team.

Saturn is Jupiter's guest in your rising sign, and it gives your big-hearted manner a more serious tone. You may notice you're quieter at gatherings, or thinking before you speak, which isn't your habit. The Ten of Wands, Saturn's decan in Sagittarius, suggests you might be carrying more than people realise as well, helping everyone and showing up cheerful while quietly overloaded.

In a friendship group it could be a falling-out, or finding you've been left out of something. At work it might be a frank remark in a meeting that didn't go down well. In a new relationship, watch how you talk about your past. Ask yourself honestly whether one group you belong to still feels like yours. If it doesn't, you can step back without making a speech.
rising.reversed:
Tact tends to go missing when a Sagittarius Ascendant draws this card reversed. Jupiter's guest, turned upside down, says the first true thing that comes to mind and doesn't stop to see where it lands. The cheerful frankness tips into blurting, a comment about someone's divorce at a party, a joke about a sore subject. Or you keep things so upbeat that nobody's allowed to be sad around you, and people feel you haven't really heard them.

At work it can be the throwaway line that turns into a grievance. With a new friend it's the story told at their expense. With family it's breezing in and out without noticing who's struggling. Ask extra questions in the next few conversations and hold back one opinion each time. You'll hear a lot that way, and you'll probably find out what's been going on.

sun.upright:
Saturn rules Capricorn. So when this card, a Saturn card, is drawn for a Capricorn Sun, it speaks with the authority of your sign's own landlord. It isn't a random hurt. It's the sort of lesson your chart is built to take seriously, about what holds and what doesn't. Capricorn Suns want to build something solid and be respected for it, and you can take a lot of pressure. What this card brings is a different weight, the hurt that comes from a relationship, a partnership, somebody you counted on.

Libra squares Capricorn, both cardinal, and friction between them forces action. The classic version for a Capricorn Sun is work pulling against love. You've been building the career, keeping everything going, and something on the other side has quietly given way. Air against earth adds to it. You trust what people do over what they say, and it's a shock when the words turn out to have mattered. It feels like failure, and Capricorns hate failing. Usually it's that you were strong in one place and absent in another.

At work it might be a business partnership ending, or a boss you respected letting you down. At home it could be a partner telling you they've felt alone for a while. With your father or someone senior, it's seeing them clearly for the first time. Look honestly at the parts of your life that haven't had your attention, and give one of them an hour you'd normally give to work.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, the card can turn a Capricorn Sun's strength against itself. You deal with the hurt by working harder, and it works for a while, because Saturn at home knows how to endure. Endurance and healing are different things, though. The grief gets pushed into a corner and turns up later as coldness, as tiredness sleep doesn't fix, as a short temper with the people who most want to help.

In the office it's the extra hours and the new target set the week after something fell apart. At home it's being there in body and elsewhere in your head. With friends it's cancelling because you're busy. Put one evening in the diary for the hurt, the way you would for a meeting. Spend it doing nothing productive, and let yourself feel what comes.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safe when it's coping. Things under control, bills paid, nobody needing to see you wobble. Saturn rules Capricorn, so this card on your Moon is your own planet asking something of you. That can be oddly steadying. Hard truths are familiar ground for this Moon, and part of you trusts a painful fact over a comforting story. It can also mean the hurt goes straight into the place where you keep old ones, filed and not felt.

Capricorn is earth and the card is air, opposed elements, idea against matter. Libra squares Capricorn too, both cardinal, and a square forces action. So the sad thing and the practical thing grind against each other. Something's broken your heart a little and you're organising the logistics of it, the forms, the arrangements, the phone calls, with a lump in your throat you haven't got time for. Plenty of Capricorn Moons learned young that they had to be the grown-up. You can keep being capable and still let yourself be sad about it.

With a parent it might be an old disappointment come round again. With a partner it's being so reliable they don't realise you're hurting. In the body it tends to sit in the neck and shoulders, a stiffness you blame on the desk. Let one person do one practical thing for you, and don't check it afterwards.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on a Capricorn Moon, the card tends to freeze things. You're fine. You're really fine. The grief has been set aside for later, and later doesn't come, because there's always something more pressing. Saturn in its own sign can keep a feeling in cold storage for years, and reversed that's exactly what it does.

In the body it shows as stiffness and tiredness, and sleep that stays shallow. With family it's being the dependable one in every crisis and never the one being checked on. In a relationship it can look like distance your partner can't get past. Let a little of it thaw. Look at a photo, play the song, visit the place, and let yourself feel it for as long as it lasts, without tidying up afterwards.

rising.upright:
Work is probably where this one hurts, and with Capricorn rising you'll be the last to show it. Your Ascendant comes across as composed, serious and capable, and people assume you've got it together, which you usually do. Saturn rules your rising sign, which makes it your chart ruler, so this card carries a lot of weight in how you're meeting the world. People may see that you're carrying something, though it'll show in a set jaw and fewer jokes, and they'll rarely see a tear.

With Capricorn rising, Libra sits at the top of your chart, on the tenth house of career and public life. So the hurt is likely to be about work, reputation or standing, the job, the title, how you're seen by people who matter to you professionally. Libra squares Capricorn, both cardinal, so there's friction between how you present and what's actually going on. Air against earth, too. Someone said something about your work, or a professional relationship broke, and your composed front is answering with even more composure.

In meetings you may be quieter, more careful, holding back your usual authority. With new contacts you'll come across as reserved. A partner or close friend might notice you're tired and not saying so. Is there someone at work you'd trust with how this has really landed? If there is, ask them for a coffee.
rising.reversed:
A Capricorn Ascendant with the Three reversed can seem colder than you are. The composure turns into a wall. You answer questions briefly, you keep everything professional, and people who'd like to be kind don't know how to get near you. Or the hurt comes out as sternness, a harsh word to a junior colleague, a judgement made too quickly.

At work it's a reputation for being tough that you never set out to earn. With new people it's being respected and not much liked. With family it's being the one who handles things and never the one who gets hugged. Let one thing slip in company, a laugh or an admission that it's been a hard stretch, and let people respond.

sun.upright:
Saturn is the traditional ruler of Aquarius, with Uranus as the modern one, so this card arrives at an Aquarius Sun with a landlord's authority. It's air meeting air as well, Libra and Aquarius four signs apart in a trine, and the card speaks your language fluently. Aquarius Suns want to stand for something, to be part of something bigger, and to be seen as their own person while doing it. The hurt here is often about a group, a friend, a cause or a principle. Someone you thought shared your values turned out not to.

The Aquarian way with pain is to understand it from a distance. You can explain what happened, why it happened, what it says about people in general. That's a real strength, and the trine makes it easy. Too easy, sometimes. You can think about a hurt so thoroughly that you never quite feel it, and what's left is a cool clarity with something sore underneath that you can't reach. Saturn in its own sign gives the whole thing structure and seriousness. It wants the lesson learned properly, which means feeling it.

In friendship it could be the end of a long one, or a drifting apart you've only just admitted. In a group or organisation it might be a falling-out over principles. At work it's a colleague you backed who didn't back you. Write to the friend you've lost, even if you never send it, and say what you'd miss.
sun.reversed:
When this card is upside down for an Aquarius Sun, the detachment goes too far. You're so reasonable about the hurt that you've stopped feeling it, and people close to you find you strangely cool. Or it turns into a principle. The personal wound becomes a stance, and you're fighting for a cause when what you really need is to grieve a friend.

In groups it shows as stepping back from everything, quietly, without saying why. In love it's being pleasant and far away. At work it's the email written in perfect, icy logic. Try saying the hurt in one sentence that has the word 'I' in it and nothing about how people in general behave. Say it to the person, if you can.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon needs freedom, friends and a bit of distance to feel safe, and too much closeness makes you twitchy. This card on your Moon usually means a hurt has come through a friendship or a group, or through someone who got close and then didn't play fair. Saturn rules Aquarius in traditional astrology and is at home in your Moon's sign, strong and unforced. The card's air matches your Moon's air, the trine flows, and you'll see this with real clarity.

The pull is that an Aquarius Moon tends to step back from its own feelings and study them. What happened, what it means, what the pattern is. It's useful. It can also leave the actual sadness standing outside in the cold. Fixed air holds its views firmly once it has them, and you may have decided very quickly what this hurt is about and closed the door on feeling it any other way. It's like watching yourself be upset, a bit puzzled.

With friends it might be a group that's split, or one friend who's gone. With a partner it could be needing space when they want to comfort you. Sleep can go odd, late nights reading about the thing that happened. Let one friend get close enough to see you upset, closer than feels comfortable. You can go back to your usual distance afterwards.
moon.reversed:
An Aquarius Moon with the card reversed often goes numb. Detachment is your native move, and turned up it becomes an eerie calm, like watching your life through glass. You might argue with the grief, as if it's unreasonable to feel this much. Saturn in its own sign can hold a feeling at arm's length for a long time, and reversed it doesn't want to hand over control.

With friends it's disappearing from the group without explanation. With a partner it's the cool, logical conversation that leaves them shut out. Your body shows it as restlessness and odd sleep. Find something that moves you without being about you. A film, a piece of music, a story about a stranger. Let it get to you, and follow the feeling back to where it started.

rising.upright:
Something you believed in has let you down, and it's showing in how you meet people. Aquarius rising comes across as friendly and a little detached, interesting and hard to pin down. With this card on your Ascendant, Saturn, your traditional chart ruler, is making itself felt at the front door. People may find you more serious, more guarded, more obviously thoughtful. With Aquarius rising, Libra falls on your ninth house, the house of beliefs, study and far-off places, and the two signs are trine, air to air.

So the hurt shaping how you meet people may be about what you believe. A course, a teacher, a trip, a faith or a philosophy that's let you down. You might feel estranged from your usual ideals, as if the big picture you used to talk about so easily has gone dim. Fixed air likes to hold its ground, and there's a pull to hang onto old views even when the hurt is telling you they need adjusting. People might pick up a sharper edge in your opinions, or notice you're quiet about causes that normally fire you up.

In study or travel it could be a plan that's fallen through. With new people it's being less sure of yourself when the conversation turns to ideas. In friendship groups you're watching more than joining. Which of your beliefs has this hurt actually changed? Say the updated version out loud to someone you trust.
rising.reversed:
Friendly distance can harden into aloofness on an Aquarius Ascendant when the card's reversed. Saturn at home on your Ascendant makes the coolness look like principle, which makes it harder to spot. People meet someone polite and unreachable, clever and hard to warm to. Or you go the other way and your opinions come out sharp and cold, as if the hurt has turned into a position everyone has to agree with.

In meetings it's being right and not quite trusted. In new friendships it's seeming interesting but distant. Online it might be the debate you keep having with strangers when the real argument is with someone you know. Leave one argument unfinished. Let the other person have the last word, and put that energy into a conversation with somebody you care about.

sun.upright:
A clear, cold truth has arrived in a life that mostly works by feeling its way. Pisces Suns are here to feel for others, to imagine, to blur the line between themselves and whatever they love. This is an air card, sharp and exact, and your Sun is water, soft and without edges. Air and water are neutral to each other and have to be introduced, so the card can feel like an intrusion.

Saturn has no rank in Pisces and takes its colour from Jupiter, or Neptune if you use the modern ruler, which lets the hurt spread wide. You might not be able to say where your sadness ends and someone else's begins. Saturn does rule the first ten degrees of Pisces, though, the decan of the Eight of Cups, a figure walking away from eight cups at night towards the hills. That's the edge in this card for you. Some of this hurt is about seeing clearly that something you've poured yourself into isn't going to fill back up, and that leaving might be part of the answer. There's sorrow in that, mixed with a tired sort of relief.

In a relationship it could be admitting you've been doing all the rescuing. At work it might be a caring role that's taken a great deal and given little back. With a friend who always needs you, it's noticing the pattern at last. Picture walking away from one thing that drains you. You don't have to go. Just see how it feels to imagine it.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with this card reversed can soak up hurt that isn't even theirs. Everyone's sorrow becomes yours, and your own gets lost in the mix. Or you drift away from it, into sleep, screens, daydreams, anything that softens the edges. Jupiter and Neptune make it easy to float, and Saturn upside down gives you nothing firm to stand on.

On the job this can be the colleague whose problems you've taken home every night. In love it's forgiving the same thing again and again. In the family it's being the sponge in every crisis. Set one small boundary and keep it. A time you stop answering messages, a subject you won't discuss, a visit you'll make shorter. Notice that nothing terrible happens.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon feels everything, including a lot that belongs to other people. You need gentleness, quiet, and time alone to wring out the day. This card on your Moon means something sharp has got into that soft place. Maybe a cold, clear truth, maybe a hurt you absorbed from someone close. Pisces is mutable water, ruled by Jupiter, or Neptune in modern astrology, and neither is much good with edges.

Libra and Pisces are quincunx, two signs that share nothing and keep having to make small adjustments to each other, and that's what this feels like. The card's clean, spoken hurt and your Moon's wordless, oceanic feeling keep shuffling round each other. You may cry without knowing exactly why. You may know exactly why and not be able to cry. Saturn's foothold in Pisces is the Eight of Cups, the card of leaving at night, and a Pisces Moon's first instinct when hurt is often to disappear, into sleep, into music, into your own head.

Sleep is where it shows most, long and heavy or broken and full of dreams. With a partner it might be needing solitude and feeling guilty about it. With friends it's being the one everyone brings their troubles to when you've got troubles of your own. Keep a notebook by the bed. When you wake up sad, write down the dream or the feeling before it slips away, and let that be the only thing you do with it.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on a Pisces Moon, the hurt often goes into the fog. You drift, you sleep too much, you escape into shows or daydreams or other people's dramas. You feel it all, so much that you can't look at it directly. Or you take it all on yourself, as though every sad thing that happened was somehow yours to fix.

At home it might be long evenings on the sofa with the curtains drawn. With a partner it's absorbing their mood and losing track of your own. With friends it's saying yes to every crisis call. Find one clear edge. A walk at the same time every morning, a meal at a proper table, a set bedtime. Something with a shape to it helps the feeling settle.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly. You look approachable and a bit dreamy, and strangers tell you their troubles in the queue at the chemist. With this card at your door there's a sadness in how you're coming across, and people who are hurting themselves will find you. Air and water have no natural bond, and the card's sharp clarity sits oddly on a face that usually shows everything in soft focus.

With Pisces rising, Libra falls on your eighth house, the house of intimacy, shared money and endings. So the hurt probably sits somewhere private and deep, in a close bond, in something shared that's come apart, or in a loss. Libra and Pisces are quincunx, which means constant small adjustments between what's happening underneath and how you present. You may find you're moved very easily, tearing up at an advert, at a bit of kindness. Saturn has a foothold in your sign through the Eight of Cups, the card of walking away, and some of what shows on your face is that pull.

At work you may be the one colleagues bring their problems to, just when you have least to give. On a first date you might come across as lovely and a bit far away. With strangers you'll be kind and easily drained. Choose who gets your softness for a while. It's fine to be pleasant and brief with people who take a lot.
rising.reversed:
A Pisces Ascendant with the card reversed can be hard to reach. You're there in body and drifting in mind, friendly and vague, and people can't get hold of what you think. Or you take on the sadness of everyone you meet and go home wrung out, with nothing left for your own. Saturn is only a guest in Pisces, and reversed it lets the edges go altogether.

At work it's missing details because you're elsewhere in your head. With new people it's being liked and forgotten, because nothing clear was said. In love it's picking up someone else's hurt and calling it closeness. Before a meeting or a social thing, decide one clear thing you want to say, and say it early. Then let the rest of the conversation be as soft as it likes.

1.upright:
Your face, your body, the way you walk into a room and start things, all of that belongs to the first house. With this card here, a hurt has got into how you carry yourself. The first house is Aries's natural territory, and Saturn is in fall in Aries, which means the planet of weight and limits struggles to be heard there. So the card's lesson doesn't sit easily in this house. It tends to arrive through the body and the mood before you've understood it.

Libra, the card's sign, is opposite Aries. The first and seventh houses are two ends of one line, you and the other person, and this card pulls hard towards the seventh. Whatever's hurting probably involves someone else, and it's changed how you see yourself. You might feel less sure of your own outline. You catch yourself in a shop window looking sadder than you feel, or feel sadder than you look. Air and fire get on, so there's energy in it too, a sharp clarity about who you are and who you won't be again.

In the body it may show as tiredness or a change in how you hold yourself. With new beginnings, a job or a project, you might hesitate where you'd usually leap. With your appearance it can be wanting a change, a haircut, a different way of dressing. Do something for your body that isn't about fixing it. A long bath, a swim, a proper meal eaten slowly.
1.reversed:
In the first house, the reversed card often shows in the body before you've admitted anything. Shoulders up round your ears, a set jaw, a way of walking into rooms as if you're expecting a knock. You're brisk and fine and quick to change the subject, and the effort of looking unbothered is wearing you out. Mars, this house's natural ruler, is happy to keep the armour on indefinitely.

It shows in how you start things, cautiously, half expecting them to go wrong. With new people it's either telling them all about what happened in the first ten minutes or telling them nothing at all. Stand up straight, drop your shoulders, and next time you introduce yourself, lead with something you like doing. Notice how differently people respond.

2.upright:
The second house is the money you actually have and what you think you're worth, and those two are more tangled than most people admit. With this card in the second, there's a loss or a hard truth about resources. A payment that didn't come through, a plan for the money that has to be let go, or the moment you realised you'd been undervaluing yourself for years. Taurus is this house's natural sign, fixed earth ruled by Venus, and the card is air. Those elements are opposed. Words against proof, promises against what's in the bank.

Libra and Taurus are quincunx, so the adjustment between what you hoped for and what you've got is slow and fiddly. Both signs are ruled by Venus, which is the one link between them, and it means the hurt is often about value as much as money. What something was worth to you, what you were worth to someone. It can feel like shame, even when there's nothing shameful about it. A lot of people go quiet about money when it hurts, and the quiet makes it heavier.

With income it might be a pay rise that didn't come, or work that isn't paid what it's worth. With possessions it could be losing something you valued, or having to sell it. With self-worth it's the comment that made you doubt what you bring. Sit down with the actual numbers, calmly, and write down what's true. Then write three things you're good at that have nothing to do with money.
2.reversed:
A money hurt that's being avoided is the usual story when this card falls reversed in the second house. Bills unopened, a balance not checked, a loss nobody's allowed to mention. Or the grief comes out as spending, comfort purchases, the treat that makes up for something else. Fixed earth holds onto things, and sometimes that includes a financial disappointment that could have been dealt with long ago.

With income it can be a job you stay in out of fear. With possessions it's keeping things that belonged to a time or a person you've lost. With self-worth it's accepting less than you deserve because asking feels risky. Open the envelope, or the app, and look. The number is usually less frightening once it's known, and you can make a plan from there.

3.upright:
Messages, conversations, siblings, neighbours, the short trips and the things you pick up along the way, that's the third house. It's Gemini's natural house, and Libra trines Gemini, air to air, so this card is at ease here. Possibly too much at ease, because the same element doubles everything. The hurt in this card comes through words, and in the third house words are everywhere. A message you shouldn't have read, something a sibling said, a remark in the corridor that won't leave you alone.

The Moon has its joy in this house, so feelings run close to the surface in everyday conversation, and a small comment can carry a lot. You might catch yourself replaying a conversation, rewriting what you said, drafting the reply you never sent. Mental energy going round and round. The trine means the words for this come easily, and you may already have said more about it than you meant to.
